name: bruteforce-salted-openssl
summary: Try to find the password of a file that was encrypted with the 'openssl' command.
highlights: -1 — Stop the program after finding the first password candidate.
-a — List the available cipher and digest algorithms.
-B — Search using binary passwords (instead of character passwords). Write candidates to <file>
-D — Display salt, key and iv along with the tested password.
-d — Digest for key and initialization vector generation. default: sha256

flags.description: Stop the program after finding the first password candidate.

flags.name: -a
flags.description: List the available cipher and digest algorithms.

flags.name: -B
flags.description: Search using binary passwords (instead of character passwords). Write candidates to <file>.

flags.name: -b
flags.description: Beginning of the password. default: ""

flags.name: -c
flags.description: Cipher for decryption. default: aes-256-cbc

flags.name: -D
flags.description: Display salt, key and iv along with the tested password.

flags.name: -d
flags.description: Digest for key and initialization vector generation. default: sha256

flags.name: -e
flags.description: End of the password. default: ""

flags.name: -f
flags.description: Read the passwords from a file instead of generating them.

flags.name: -h
flags.description: Show help and quit.

flags.name: -i
flags.description: With -K, set the PBKDF2 iteration count to <n>. default: 10000

flags.name: -K
flags.description: Use PKCS5_PBKDF2_HMAC to derive the key.

flags.name: -L
flags.description: Limit the maximum number of tested passwords to <n>.

flags.name: -l
flags.description: Minimum password length (beginning and end included). default: 1

flags.name: -M
flags.description: Consider the decryption as successful when the data starts with <string>. Without this option, the decryption is considered as successful when the data contains mostly printable ASCII characters (at least 90%).

flags.name: -m
flags.description: Maximum password length (beginning and end included). default: 8

flags.name: -N
flags.description: Ignore decryption errors (similar to openssl -nopad).

flags.name: -n
flags.description: Ignore salt (similar to openssl -nosalt).

flags.name: -p
flags.description: Preview and check the first N decrypted bytes for the magic string. If the magic string is present, try decrypting the rest of the data. default: 1024

flags.name: -s
flags.description: Password character set. default: "0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTU VWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"

flags.name: -t
flags.description: Number of threads to use. default: 1

flags.name: -v
flags.description: Print progress info every n seconds.

flags.name: -w
flags.description: Restore the state of a previous session if the file exists, then write the state to the file regularly (~ every minute).
